root_cause: MEMORY EXHAUSTION. Not hardware, not a version regression, not silent corruption.

evidence.resource_exhaustion_events: 40 Microsoft-Windows-Resource-Exhaustion-Detector (event 2004, 'low virtual memory') since 2026-07-23, escalating: 1 on 07-26, 1 on 07-27, 10 on 07-28, 7 on 07-29, and 16 TODAY (07-30) — the day of the failures.
evidence.most_recent_event: 2026-07-30 20:23:42 — 'vmmemWSL consumed 3,977,756,672 bytes, firefox.exe 1,934,340,096 bytes, python.exe 1,171,828,736 bytes'.
evidence.memory: TotalVisible 7,739 MB; Free 393 MB at time of check. vmmemWSL alone holds ~4 GB.
evidence.uptime: 6 days 7 hours (last boot 2026-07-24 13:09), so pressure has accumulated since before the bge published run.
evidence.no_hardware_signature: NO WHEA and NO machine-check entries in Application or System since 2026-07-23. The hardware hypothesis is ruled out, not merely unlikely.

explains_every_observation.model_size_dependence: bge-base is ~110M params (~440 MB fp32) against MiniLM's ~22M. Only the larger model exceeds what is free.
explains_every_observation.batch_size_dependence: batch 8 succeeded 4/4 with zero crashes; batch 64 failed 8/8. Peak activation memory scales with batch size.
explains_every_observation.intermittency: free memory fluctuates with other processes, so the same operation succeeds or fails depending on the moment.
explains_every_observation.escalating_failure_rate: 16 low-memory events today; my own repeated runs added to the pressure they were failing against.
explains_every_observation.why_2026_07_26_worked: one low-memory event that day against sixteen today.
explains_every_observation.fail_stop_behaviour: an allocation failure is fail-stop by construction, which is exactly what the section-1 probe measured: 4/4 successes bit-identical.

blast_radius.bounded: Memory exhaustion cannot silently corrupt a completed computation — it prevents one. Combined with the fail-stop probe, no computed number on this machine is in question on account of this fault.
blast_radius.positive_control: family-1 MiniLM re-runs reproduced 0.5682 / 0.7216 and Track B's levels EXACTLY today, on this machine, under this pressure.
blast_radius.published_bge: run-20260726-191447 ran on a day with ONE low-memory event. Unverified at the encoding step, but there is no mechanism by which this fault would have perturbed it rather than crashed it.

remedy: Free memory. vmmemWSL holds ~4 GB and firefox ~1.9 GB; releasing either would very likely make bge encodable immediately. Cheaper and less disruptive than a reboot, but both are the operator's call — shutting down WSL would terminate the user's sessions.
progress: checkpoint/resume is live and 4 batches are already banked permanently; each needs to succeed once, ever.
